The upper side of the upper-left rectangle is marked 11, and the upper side of the lower-right rectangle is marked 13. There are two internal cutting lines in the figure, both starting from the lower-left corner and respectively connecting to the black dot at the upper stair turning point and the black dot on the right vertical side. The right side shows these three pieces reassembled into a large triangle, and the original edges and cutting lines form one horizontal line and one vertical line inside the triangle. Reasoning: Tracking according to lengths, in the left figure the horizontal width of the left rectangle is 11, and the horizontal width of the right rectangle is 13, so the total width at the bottom of the original figure is 11 + 13 = 24. After being reassembled into the triangle on the right, the vertical side originally marked x is rotated and corresponds to a long horizontal side segment in the triangle. This long horizontal side segment is composed of two parts: one part corresponds to the original upper side of the right rectangle, 13, and the other part corresponds to the entire bottom width of the original figure, 24. Therefore x = 13 + 24 = 13 + 11 + 13 = 37.
